headline: The Elementary School Building Committee narrowed Neary School design options, while the Select Board took positions on Special Town Meeting warrant articles.
synopsis: The Elementary School Building Committee voted to eliminate Option 4 for the Neary School project and instructed consultants to study Options 1, 3, and a 15 million dollar baseline ahead of Fall Town Meeting. The Select Board reopened the October 17 Special Town Meeting warrant, voting to support revised articles on two-family housing and an irrigation project while voting against a trail cleanup article. The Municipal Technology Committee finalized plans to launch the 2026 town satisfaction survey on October 1, working in collaboration with the Affordable Housing Trust on survey questions. Additionally, the Affordable Housing Trust explored investing roughly 1 million dollars in idle funds into higher-yield options and continued drafting a 55-plus housing bylaw.

highlights.title: Neary School Option 4 eliminated as costs are reviewed
highlights.why: The committee voted 3-1 to drop Option 4 and voted 4-0 to direct consultants to focus on Options 1, 3, and a 15 million dollar baseline after preliminary project costs were estimated between 24.4 million and 49.2 million dollars.

highlights.title: Select Board votes recommendations on Special Town Meeting articles
highlights.why: The board voted 5-0 to support revised Article 2 on two-family housing and Article 3 on an irrigation project, but voted 1-4 against supporting Article 4 for trail cleanup before reclosing the warrant.

highlights.title: Affordable Housing Trust explores investing 1 million dollars in cash
highlights.why: Trustees learned that holding approximately 1 million dollars in near-zero interest accounts has forgone substantial returns over past years and agreed to consult town finance officials regarding higher-yield investment options.

highlights.title: 2026 Town Satisfaction Survey prepared for October launch
highlights.why: The committee finalized question adjustments to reduce survey drop-offs and added questions on affordable housing and senior services ahead of an October 1 to November 30 survey run.

highlights.title: Educators favor Option 3 for Neary site plan
highlights.why: Architects presented feedback from first responders, public works, and staff, highlighting strong educator support for Option 3 because it encloses the courtyard for a gymnasium and keeps existing play fields intact.

looking_ahead.what: Select Board meeting covering financial policies and Breakneck Hill debt reduction
